description: Machine-readable module dependency manifest. Mirrors docs/phase-3/01-system-architecture.md §3.3. Consumed by eslint/index.js to build import/no-restricted-paths zones. Every source root under packages/server/src is one of: shared-kernel | platform | domain | accounting-core | isolated. Extend this file as new modules land — do not hand-edit the ESLint rule itself.

platform/auth.note: Module 1 boundary decision (see docs/phase-5 Module 1 report): auth is granted a deliberate one-directional dependency on platform/users — usr_user/usr_session/usr_login_event/usr_password_history/usr_api_key are auth-lifecycle tables but the usr_user/usr_role/usr_permission *entities* (schema truth) live under platform/users/domain per module 1's file layout. By convention (not yet mechanically enforced by this manifest — see crossSiblingImportPolicy below) auth only imports platform/users/domain/*.entity.ts and the platform/users barrel (index.ts) — never users' application/infrastructure internals directly. platform/users itself imports shared only; there is no reverse edge, so this is not a cycle.

platform/users.note: platform modules may depend on shared-kernel only; sibling platform modules (e.g. platform/auth) are off-limits except via their public index/exports, enforced as importableViaIndexOnly below

platform/settings.note: platform modules may depend on shared-kernel only by default (architecture doc §3.3 rule 2). Settings has no legitimate need to reach into auth/users internals — its RBAC codes live as plain string literals in @RequirePermission(...) decorators, validated at runtime against the DB-seeded usr_permission table, not via a compile-time import of platform/users' catalogue.

platform/files.note: Same precedent as platform/auth (see its note above): files is granted a deliberate one-directional dependency on platform/users for the file_object.uploaded_by FK target only. By convention files only imports platform/users/domain/usr-user.entity.ts directly — never users' application/infrastructure internals. platform/users itself imports shared only, so this is not a cycle.

platform/branding.note: brnd_theme.logo_file_id/favicon_file_id FK to file_object, so branding is granted a deliberate one-directional dependency on platform/files (imports FileObjectEntity via its index.ts barrel only, per crossSiblingImportPolicy — see platform/files' index.ts doc comment, which names Branding as its first documented consumer). Also granted a one-directional dependency on platform/auth, same precedent as platform/auth's own note on platform/users: branding's public GET /branding/theme/current endpoint (served to the login page before authentication, FR-BRND-002.1) needs to opt out of the auth guard pipeline via the already-established @Public() decorator (platform/auth/infrastructure/guards/public.decorator.ts) rather than duplicating that mechanism; branding imports only Public via platform/auth's index.ts barrel, never auth's application/infrastructure internals. Neither platform/files nor platform/auth import branding, so this is not a cycle.

platform/comms.note: Module 5 (Communications). Same one-directional-dependency precedent as platform/auth -> platform/users: comm_device_token.user_id FKs to usr_user (imported via platform/users' index.ts barrel only), and BroadcastsService resolves STAFF_ROLE/EXPLICIT_USER_IDS audience_def kinds against UsersService.listActiveUsersByRoleId()/.listByIds() (the module's public surface, never its repositories/infrastructure internals) — guardian/parent audience kinds are deferred to Module 8 (Students), which doesn't exist yet. Also granted a one-directional dependency on platform/settings: AdapterResolverService asks settings' IntegrationConfigService (public service only) for the enabled SMTP/SMS/FCM set_integration_config row backing the real adapters (GenericHttpSmsAdapter/SmtpMailAdapter/FcmPushAdapter), falling back to comms' own LogOnlyAdapter when none is enabled. Neither platform/users nor platform/settings import platform/comms, so this is not a cycle.

platform/document-verification.note: Phase 6 Slice 16 (Part 1 — Document Security: Watermark + QR Verification backend). A fully generic module — module-deps.json's own default (shared-kernel only) is extended with exactly one exception, the same one-directional-dependency precedent platform/branding's own mayImport entry documents for its public GET /branding/theme/current route: DocumentVerificationController's one route (GET /document-verification/:token) uses the already-established @Public() decorator (platform/auth/infrastructure/guards/public.decorator.ts, imported via platform/auth's index.ts barrel only, never auth's application/infrastructure internals) to opt out of the JWT auth guard pipeline — an anonymous QR-code scanner holds no credentials at all. docv_record.document_type/.document_id are a deliberately loose, FK-less polymorphic reference (same convention appr_instance.entity_type/.entity_id and comm_message.entity_type/.entity_id already establish) specifically so this module never needs a mayImport entry for any domain module that might ever mint a token — DocumentVerificationService.mint(em, ...) takes the CALLER's own transaction EntityManager (same in-transaction-composability convention platform/settings' NumberingService.allocate(em, ...) established) rather than this module reaching into the caller's own tables. platform/auth does not import platform/document-verification back, so this is not a cycle.

platform/approvals.note: Module 6 (Approvals). Same one-directional-dependency precedent as platform/auth -> platform/users: appr_level.role_id/appr_routing_rule.department_id/appr_instance.initiator_id/appr_action.actor_id/appr_delegation.from_user_id+to_user_id all FK to usr_role/usr_department/usr_user (imported via platform/users' index.ts barrel only), and ApprovalEngineService's ROLE/DEPT_HEAD approver checks call UsersService.listActiveUsersByRoleId()/DepartmentsService.findByIdOrFail() (the module's public surface, never its repositories/infrastructure internals). UsersService.hasRole() was also added for this module (same pattern as listByIds()/listActiveUsersByRoleId() being added for platform/comms) but ended up unused by ApprovalEngineService itself, kept as a small independently-useful public-surface addition. platform/users itself imports shared only, so this is not a cycle. ApprovalEngineService is this module's whole reason to exist — every future domain module (billing, payments, procurement, payroll, journal entries) is expected to import platform/approvals' index.ts barrel and call submit()/getStatus() inside its own transaction, mirroring how platform/settings' NumberingService.allocate() is consumed.

accounting.note: Module 7 application pass. Same one-directional-dependency precedent as platform/auth -> platform/users: accounting core is granted two deliberate exceptions to the architecture doc §3.3 rule 2 default (shared kernel only), both grouped conceptually with accounting core in the docs/phase-3/01-system-architecture.md §3.3 C4 diagram or required for budget approval. (1) platform/settings: PostingService.post() calls NumberingService.allocate(em, 'GL_JOURNAL') for gapless journal numbering — set_numbering_series is general-purpose across every doc type in the system and its set_ table prefix correctly keeps it under Settings rather than duplicating a numbering allocator inside accounting core. (2) platform/approvals: BudgetsService.submitForApproval() calls ApprovalEngineService.submit() to attach a GL_BUDGET approval instance to a gl_budget row before it can go ACTIVE. Both imports are one-directional and go only through each module's public service exports (platform/settings' NumberingService, platform/approvals' ApprovalEngineService, both via their index.ts barrels) — never their repositories/domain/infrastructure internals. Neither platform/settings nor platform/approvals imports accounting, so this is not a cycle.

domains/students.note: Module 8 (Students) — the first domains/* module. Narrower than domainModuleDefaults' generic "platform/*" wildcard placeholder below, per that block's own instruction to register a concrete entry once a domain module exists. Five exceptions to the shared-kernel-only default, all entity-only (no sibling *service* is called at runtime, unlike accounting's platform/settings+platform/approvals imports): (1) accounting — reserved for a future domain-module convention (none of this pass's entities/services reach into it yet; kept for parity with domainModuleDefaults' documented allowance and because StudentLedgerService.appendEntry() is explicitly designed for future Billing/Payments callers to invoke inside their own accounting-core posting transaction). (2) platform/settings — std_promotion_batch.from_year_id/to_year_id are real FKs to set_academic_year (imported via platform/settings' index.ts barrel only). (3) platform/files — std_student.photo_file_id is a real FK to file_object (imported via platform/files' index.ts barrel only). (4) platform/users — std_guardian.user_id is a real FK to usr_user, the portal-account link (imported via platform/users' index.ts barrel only). (5) domains/billing — added by Module 9 (Billing)'s foundation pass: std_student.sponsor_id/.transport_route_id are now real FKs to bill_sponsor/bill_transport_route (BillSponsorEntity/BillTransportRouteEntity, nothing else), closing the forward-reference gap Module 8 left open (see std-student.entity.ts's doc comment and migration 0071). None of platform/settings, platform/files, or platform/users import domains/students, so those three remain non-cyclic. domains/billing DOES import domains/students (real FKs to std_student/std_class/std_stream/std_fee_group, per its own mayImport entry below) — this exception (5) makes the students<->billing relationship DELIBERATELY BIDIRECTIONAL at the entity level, an unusual shape for this codebase's normal 'domain modules don't import each other' rule (domainModuleDefaults' note), called out explicitly here and in domains/billing's own entry: each direction is narrowly scoped to specific FK-target entities, never full sibling internals, and is justified by the schema's own design coupling students and billing tightly via the sponsor/transport-route references. IMPORTANT DEVIATION from crossSiblingImportPolicy's normal 'index.ts/*.module.ts only' rule, for this bidirectional pair specifically: both sides import the other's entities directly from their entity FILES (e.g. '../../billing/domain/bill-sponsor.entity', not '../../billing'), not through the barrel/module.ts. Importing through either barrel was tried first and produced a genuine circular-require crash at test-run time ('A circular dependency has been detected inside @InjectRepository()') — a barrel's first export is its *Module class, which eagerly pulls in the whole sibling module's controllers/services/repositories (NestJS's @InjectRepository(Entity) needs the entity class value eagerly, unlike TypeORM's @ManyToOne(() => Entity) thunks), turning this narrow entity-level FK cycle into a module-graph cycle. Direct entity-file imports (both directions) avoid ever loading the sibling's module.ts/controllers as a side effect of loading an entity, eliminating the crash while preserving the FK relationship — documented on both import statements themselves (std-student.entity.ts and every domains/billing entity file that references StdStudentEntity/StdClassEntity/StdStreamEntity/StdFeeGroupEntity).

domains/billing.note: Module 9 (Billing) — PASS A of the application-layer pass now landed on top of the foundation pass (entities/repositories/migration/triggers only; docs/phase-5/PROGRESS.md). Four foundation-pass exceptions remain entity-only (no sibling *service* called at runtime): (1) accounting — bill_fee_category.gl_income_account_id/bill_concession_scheme.gl_account_id/bill_invoice.journal_id/bill_concession.journal_id/bill_credit_note.journal_id/bill_debit_note.journal_id/bill_refund_voucher.journal_id are real FKs to gl_account/gl_journal (imported via accounting's index.ts barrel only). (2) platform/settings — bill_fee_structure.academic_year_id/.term_id, bill_student_optional_item.term_id, bill_invoice.term_id, bill_sponsor_award.term_id are real FKs to set_academic_year/set_term (imported via platform/settings' index.ts barrel only). (3) platform/files — bill_sponsor.agreement_file_id is a real FK to file_object (imported via platform/files' index.ts barrel only). (4) domains/students — bill_fee_structure.class_id/.stream_id/.fee_group_id, bill_student_optional_item.student_id, bill_invoice.student_id, bill_concession.student_id, bill_sponsor_award.student_id, bill_debit_note.student_id, bill_refund_voucher.student_id are all real FKs to std_class/std_stream/std_fee_group/std_student, BIDIRECTIONAL at the entity level with domains/students' own entry (see that entry's note for the full rationale, INCLUDING the direct-entity-file-import deviation from crossSiblingImportPolicy this pair required to avoid a real circular-require crash). PASS A adds a FIFTH exception, now a real runtime *service* dependency, not just entity-only: (5) platform/approvals — ConcessionsService.requestConcession() calls ApprovalEngineService.submit(em, {domainCode:'BILLING_CONCESSION', ...}) inside its own transaction, imported via platform/approvals' index.ts barrel only (never its repositories/infrastructure internals), the exact same one-directional-dependency shape accounting's own mayImport entry already established for the identical reason (BudgetsService.submitForApproval()). platform/users is still deliberately NOT in this list — approval_ref/voided_by/published_by columns throughout this module remain loose uuid columns with no FK (see each entity's doc comment). PASS A's new application services (fee-structures, invoicing/posting engine, concessions, sponsors/awards, bulk billing) call accounting's PostingService/GlAccountRepository, platform/settings' NumberingService, and domains/students' StudentLedgerService/StdStudentRepository — all already-sanctioned entries, now exercised at runtime via billing.module.ts importing AccountingModule/SettingsModule/ApprovalsModule/StudentsModule (not just their entities). PASS B (credit/debit notes, refund vouchers, late fees, controllers, permission catalogue, seed) is still pending. **New (Phase 6 Slice 16 Part 1, 2026-08-07): (6) platform/document-verification** — a SIXTH, one-directional exception, real runtime *service* dependency: FeeStructuresService.publish() calls DocumentVerificationService.mint(em, {...}) (imported via platform/document-verification's index.ts barrel only, never its repository/entity internals) inside the SAME publish() transaction, immediately after the structure's status is flipped to PUBLISHED and saved — mints an opaque verification token for the newly-published structure, minted exactly once per publish (never on create/list/find), so a DRAFT or never-published structure correctly has no token. FeeStructuresController's existing GET :id path additionally calls DocumentVerificationService.findByDocument('FEE_STRUCTURE', id) to surface an already-minted token on FeeStructureResponseDto.verificationToken without denormalizing a new column onto bill_fee_structure (an immutable-once-published financial entity, per this codebase's own established discipline). platform/document-verification does not import domains/billing back (it imports platform/auth only, per its own mayImport entry), so this is not a cycle.

domains/payments.note: Module 10 (Payments) — foundation pass + PASS A (core receipt engine) + PASS B (M-Pesa STK/C2B/B2C, suspense matching, cheque clearing, bulk allocation, ALL controllers, permission catalogue, seed) + Module 11 (Wallet)'s gap-closure migration `0091`, which added `domains/wallet` to this list: `pay_mpesa_transaction.wallet_transaction_id` is now a real FK to `wall_transaction` (`WallTransactionEntity` imported directly from its entity file, never through `domains/wallet`'s barrel — same circular-require-avoidance discipline every other cross-domain FK in this codebase follows), closing this module's own long-flagged forward-reference gap. This makes wallet<->payments bidirectional at the entity level (see `domains/wallet`'s own entry for the full rationale) — `domains/payments` itself gained no new runtime *service* dependency on `domains/wallet` (the receipt-capture WALLET-split stretch goal was NOT attempted this pass; `ReceiptsService.captureReceipt()` still rejects `WALLET` splits, see Module 11's PROGRESS.md row). Original five foundation-pass exceptions, all entity-only: (1) accounting — pay_receipt.journal_id is a real FK to gl_journal (imported via accounting's index.ts barrel only). (2) platform/settings — NumberingService.allocate()/SettingsService.getTyped() real runtime calls from PASS A onward. (3) platform/users — pay_cashier_session.cashier_id/.supervisor_id, pay_receipt.cashier_id, pay_suspense_item.resolved_by are real FKs to usr_user (imported via platform/users' index.ts barrel only). (4) domains/students — pay_receipt.student_id, pay_bulk_allocation_batch_line.student_id are real FKs to std_student, StdStudentRepository/StudentLedgerService real runtime calls from PASS A onward. (5) domains/billing — pay_receipt_allocation.invoice_id/.installment_id are real FKs to bill_invoice/bill_installment, BillInvoiceRepository/BillInstallmentRepository/resolveControlAccount/InvoicingService real runtime calls from PASS A/PASS B onward. Exceptions (4) and (5) follow the EXACT SAME direct-entity-file-import discipline Module 9 (Billing) established (StdStudentEntity/BillInvoiceEntity/BillInstallmentEntity imported directly from their own entity files, never through domains/students'/domains/billing's barrels, to avoid the same 'circular dependency detected inside @InjectRepository()' crash). PASS B adds two more exceptions: (6) platform/approvals — ReceiptsController's reverse-approval-chain and SuspenseController's refund-approval-chain both call ApprovalEngineService.submit()/getStatus() (imported via platform/approvals' index.ts barrel only) to attach/verify a PAYMENT_REVERSALS appr_instance before ReceiptsService.reverseReceipt()/SuspenseService.refundSuspenseItem() run — the exact same one-directional-dependency shape domains/billing's own mayImport entry already established for ConcessionsService/CreditNotesService/RefundVouchersService/LateFeeBatchesService. (7) platform/auth — MpesaController's four Safaricom-inbound callback endpoints (STK/C2B validation/C2B confirmation/B2C result) use the already-established @Public() decorator (platform/auth/infrastructure/guards/public.decorator.ts, imported via platform/auth's index.ts barrel only) to opt out of the JWT auth guard pipeline, since Safaricom cannot hold a JWT — same precedent platform/branding's own mayImport entry documents for its public theme endpoint. Neither platform/approvals nor platform/auth import domains/payments, so neither is a cycle. Unlike the students<->billing pair, the students/billing relationship with domains/payments is NOT bidirectional — neither domains/students nor domains/billing imports anything from domains/payments. One forward-reference gap of the two originally flagged here has since closed: pay_mpesa_transaction.wallet_transaction_id -> wall_transaction (Module 11/Wallet's own migration 0091, see domains/wallet's entry). **New: domains/banking** — Module 16 (Banking)'s migration 0141 closed the other originally-flagged gap, pay_receipt_split.bank_account_id -> bank_account, adding a real FK (BankAccountEntity imported directly from its entity file, never through domains/banking's barrel — same circular-require-avoidance discipline every other cross-domain FK in this codebase follows). domains/banking does NOT import domains/payments' module.ts/barrel back for this — it imports PayCashierSessionEntity directly from its entity file for bank_deposit/bank_withdrawal.source_session_id, making payments<->banking bidirectional at the entity level only, the same shape students<->billing/payments<->wallet already established. A third, older gap (domains/billing's own bill_refund_voucher.b2c_transaction_id -> pay_mpesa_transaction) remains open — out of this module's own scope to fix (would require editing domains/billing), still restated for whichever pass eventually closes it. **New (Phase 6 Slice 16 Part 1, 2026-08-07): (8) platform/document-verification** — an EIGHTH, one-directional exception, real runtime *service* dependency, the exact same shape this pass adds to domains/billing (see that module's own entry): ReceiptsService.captureReceipt() calls DocumentVerificationService.mint(em, {...}) (imported via platform/document-verification's index.ts barrel only) inside its own transaction, immediately after the pay_receipt row is inserted, minting an opaque verification token for every captured receipt. ReceiptsController's existing GET :id path additionally calls DocumentVerificationService.findByDocument('PAYMENT_RECEIPT', id) to surface the token on ReceiptDetailResponseDto.verificationToken without denormalizing a new column onto pay_receipt (immutable-once-posted, same discipline bill_fee_structure follows). Not called from recordSubledgerFundedReceipt()/reverseReceipt() — only captureReceipt() mints, so a wallet/credit-funded receipt or a reversal contra receipt correctly has no token of its own. platform/document-verification does not import domains/payments back, so this is not a cycle.

domains/wallet.note: Module 11 (Wallet). `mayImport` extends the task brief's own literal list (`shared`/`accounting`/`platform/settings`/`platform/approvals`/`platform/users`/`domains/students`/`domains/payments`) with `domains/billing` — a documented, deliberate addition: `wallet-control-accounts.util.ts`'s `resolveWalletControlAccount()` reuses `domains/billing`'s exported `resolveControlAccount()` (the task brief's own explicit instruction, 'reuse domains/billing's exported resolveControlAccount() from its barrel'), which is not re-exported from `domains/payments`' barrel, so `domains/billing` must be imported directly. All seven imports are real runtime *service* dependencies (not just entity-only): `accounting` (`PostingService`/`GlAccountRepository`/`GlIntegrityRunRepository` — every P-13..P-17 posting plus BR-WALL-08 reconciliation), `platform/settings` (`SettingsService.getTyped()` — BR-WALL-04 policy maxima, FR-WALL-013.1 transfer threshold), `platform/approvals` (`ApprovalEngineService.submit()`/`.getStatus()` at the controller layer — `WALLET_TRANSFER`/`WALLET_REFUND`/`WALLET_ADJUSTMENT` two-step dances), `platform/users` (`UsrUserEntity` FK target for `wall_service_point_operator.user_id`, entity-only), `domains/students` (`StdStudentEntity` — `wall_wallet.student_id` FK, direct entity-file import per the circular-require-avoidance discipline; `StdGuardianRepository` — BR-WALL-06 payout verification, real service call), `domains/billing` (`resolveControlAccount()`/`BillInvoiceRepository`/`BillInstallmentRepository` — P-15/P-16/P-17's AR-Student and WALLET control accounts, and `transferToFees()`'s invoice-allocation application), `domains/payments` (`PayReceiptEntity` — `wall_transaction.receipt_id` FK, direct entity-file import; `resolveClearingAccount()`/`PayReceiptSplitMethod` — P-13 top-up settlement-channel resolution reuse). `wall_wallet.student_id`/`wall_transaction.receipt_id`/`wall_transaction.journal_id` all follow the same direct-entity-file-import discipline Module 9/10 established (never through a sibling domain's barrel for entity-decorator targets — see each entity's own import comment) to avoid the 'circular dependency detected inside @InjectRepository()' crash. `domains/payments` also imports `domains/wallet` in the OTHER direction now (see that module's own entry, extended by this pass) — `pay_mpesa_transaction.wallet_transaction_id` is a real FK to `wall_transaction` (migration `0091`, closing Module 10's own flagged gap), making the wallet<->payments relationship DELIBERATELY BIDIRECTIONAL at the entity level, the same unusual-but-justified shape the students<->billing pair established first. Neither `platform/settings`, `platform/approvals`, `platform/users`, nor `domains/students`/`domains/billing` import `domains/wallet` back, so those remain non-cyclic; only the payments<->wallet pair is bidirectional, and only at the entity-file level (never through either's `wallet.module.ts`/`payments.module.ts`/barrel), same as students<->billing.

domains/procurement.note: Module 12 (Procurement) — foundation pass + PASS A (docs/phase-5/PROGRESS.md, see that entry for the full PASS-A writeup) + PASS B: `SupplierInvoicesService`/`PaymentVouchersService`/`ContractsService`/`SupplierRatingsService` plus every controller. `application/gl-ap-accounts.util.ts` (P-20/P-21's `AP_SUPPLIER`/`Purchase Price Variance` accounts) and `application/payment-clearing-accounts.util.ts` (P-21's per-method clearing account) both duplicate rather than import `domains/billing`'s `resolveControlAccount()`/`domains/payments`' `resolveClearingAccount()` — same `mayImport`-driven judgement call PASS A's own `gl-grn-accounts.util.ts` already made, see those two files' own doc comments. `platform/comms` — `PaymentVouchersService.execute()` calls `NotificationsService.send()` (via `platform/comms`' index.ts barrel only) for FR-PROC-008.1's remittance advice email; this is the actual home of that service (the task brief named `domains/comms`, which does not exist anywhere in this codebase — the real module lives at `platform/comms`). **New: `domains/inventory`** (Module 13's foundation pass, migration `0111` — `AddProcurementItemFks0111`) — closes the two forward-reference gaps this entry previously flagged: `proc_requisition_line.item_id`/`proc_quotation_line.item_id`/`proc_po_line.item_id` are now real, nullable FKs to `inv_item`, each entity importing `InvItemEntity` directly from its entity file (`../../inventory/domain/inv-item.entity`), never through `domains/inventory`'s barrel — the same circular-require-avoidance discipline every other cross-domain entity FK in this codebase follows (see `domains/wallet`'s entry for the precedent). This is entity-only (no sibling *service* call at runtime) — Procurement's own application services do not call into Inventory's repositories/services in this pass. `domains/inventory` does not import `domains/procurement` back, so this is not a cycle. The forward-reference gap this entry previously flagged (`proc_payment_voucher.bank_account_id`/`.cheque_leaf_id` -> `bank_account`/`bank_cheque_leaf`) is now CLOSED: **new: `domains/banking`** (Module 16's own foundation pass, migration `0142` — `AddProcurementBankFks0142`) adds both real FKs, each entity importing `BankAccountEntity`/`BankChequeLeafEntity` directly from their entity files (`../../banking/domain/bank-account.entity`/`bank-cheque-leaf.entity`), never through `domains/banking`'s barrel — the usual circular-require-avoidance discipline. `bank_cheque_leaf.voucher_id -> proc_payment_voucher` is the OTHER direction of this same relationship, built as a real FK from day one in Banking's own migration `0140` (Procurement already existed) — `BankChequeLeafEntity`'s own entity file imports `ProcPaymentVoucherEntity` directly, and `ProcPaymentVoucherEntity`'s entity file imports `BankChequeLeafEntity` directly back, a genuine two-file mutual entity import (documented as safe on both files — TypeORM relation targets are lazy thunks) rather than the usual 'diagonal' cycle via different specific files each direction (students<->billing/payments<->wallet's own shape). This makes procurement<->banking DELIBERATELY BIDIRECTIONAL at the entity level (see `domains/banking`'s own `mayImport` entry, which lists `domains/procurement` for exactly this pair) — entity-only in both directions (no sibling *service* call at runtime either way in this pass).

domains/inventory.note: Module 13 (Inventory) — foundation pass + application-layer pass (this entry updated by the application-layer pass; see docs/phase-5/PROGRESS.md's Module 13 row for the full write-up). Foundation-pass exceptions, all entity-only (no sibling *service* called at runtime): (1) `accounting` — `inv_item.gl_asset_account_id`/`.gl_expense_account_id`/`.gl_income_account_id` and `inv_movement.journal_id`/`inv_stock_take.journal_id` are real FKs to `gl_account`/`gl_journal` (imported via `accounting`'s index.ts barrel only). (2) `platform/users` — `inv_store.keeper_user_id`/`inv_transfer.issued_by`/`.received_by` are real FKs to `usr_user` (imported via `platform/users`' index.ts barrel only). `platform/settings`/`platform/approvals`, listed since the foundation pass for parity, are now REAL runtime *service* dependencies as of the application-layer pass: `NumberingService.allocate()` (`INV_TRANSFER`/`INV_STOCK_TAKE` numbering, `TransfersService`/`StockTakesService`) and `ApprovalEngineService.submit()` (`STOCK_ADJUSTMENTS` domain code, `StockTakesService.submitForApproval()`), both via their own barrels only. **New: `domains/billing`** — `gl-inventory-accounts.util.ts`'s `resolveInventoryControlAccount()` reuses `domains/billing`'s exported `resolveControlAccount()` (via its `index.ts` barrel only, never billing's application internals) rather than duplicating a local copy the way `domains/procurement`'s own `gl-grn-accounts.util.ts` had to (procurement's `mayImport` list does not include `domains/billing`) — since inventory's list DOES include it now, reuse is the correct call per this codebase's own `domains/wallet` precedent (`wallet-control-accounts.util.ts` does the exact same reuse). `domains/procurement` imports `domains/inventory` (entity-only, `InvItemEntity` — see that module's own entry) — `domains/inventory` does NOT import `domains/procurement` back, one-directional, not a cycle. Neither does `domains/billing` import `domains/inventory` back, so that pair stays one-directional too (unlike the bidirectional `domains/students`<->`domains/billing`/`domains/payments`<->`domains/wallet` pairs). `preferred_supplier_ids uuid[]` on `inv_item` stays a loose array with no FK regardless of `domains/procurement` not being in this list — a Postgres array cannot carry a real FK constraint at all, a structural limitation, not a scoping gap (same treatment `appr_level.user_ids` gets). Procurement-GRN stretch-goal integration (wiring `GrnService.post()` to call `StockMovementsService.recordReceipt()`) was NOT attempted this pass — see PROGRESS.md's Module 13 row for why and what it would need (a NEW `domains/procurement` `mayImport` entry for `domains/inventory` as a real service dependency, on top of the entity-only one it already has).

domains/expenses.note: Module 14 (Expenses) — foundation pass only (entities/repositories/migration/triggers; docs/phase-5/PROGRESS.md). domains/reporting.note: Module 18 (Reporting Engine + Dashboard) — foundation pass + PASS A (see prior note text, preserved below) + **PASS B, now ✅ COMPLETE**: the remaining 9 domain reports, `DashboardKpisService`, `MvRefreshService`, `ExportJobsService`, `ReportSchedulesService`, all `api/` controllers, the permission catalogue, and the seed. domains/integrations.note: Module 19 (Integrations) — built in a single comprehensive pass (small physical schema, 3 tables, but real mechanical substance: webhook delivery with HMAC signing/retry/auto-disable, accounting-sync adapters). DELIBERATELY NARROW scope, the opposite design point from domains/reporting's own deliberately-BROAD entry: this module TRANSMITS what other modules hand it (webhook payloads via WebhookDeliveryService.dispatch(), sync entity data via AccountingSyncService.pushEntity()) rather than independently querying other domains' data, so it never reads another domain's tables at all — no domains/* sibling appears in this mayImport list, and none ever should for this module's stated purpose. Three exceptions to the shared-kernel-only default, all real runtime *service* dependencies (never a sibling's repositories/application internals, only its index.ts barrel): (1) platform/settings — AccountingSyncResolverService calls IntegrationConfigService.list()/.getDecryptedConfig() to resolve the enabled QUICKBOOKS/XERO/SAGE set_integration_config row, the exact same pattern platform/comms' own AdapterResolverService established for SMTP/SMS/FCM. (2) platform/users — listed for parity/forward-looking readiness only (same judgement call several same-sized modules make): no intg_* table in this pass's DDL carries a real FK to usr_user (created_by/updated_by stay the standard loose uuid columns BaseEntity/MutableBaseEntity always provide, no FK constraint on either per this codebase's established convention for those two columns specifically). (3) platform/comms — WebhookDeliveryService.attemptDelivery()'s FR-INTG-007.1 auto-disable path calls NotificationsService.send() (EMAIL, to AppConfigService.integrationsAdminAlertEmail) for the admin alert, best-effort (a failed alert is logged and swallowed, never allowed to fail the triggering delivery attempt) — the same 'documented if it can't cleanly resolve' pattern domains/procurement's own PaymentVouchersService remittance-advice integration established for that same platform/comms dependency. None of platform/settings/platform/users/platform/comms imports domains/integrations back, so none of these three is a cycle. intg_sync_log.entity/.entity_id are a deliberately loose (no-FK) reference to whatever domain record is being synced — see IntgSyncLogEntity's own doc comment — precisely BECAUSE this module's mayImport list stays narrow and must not reach into every other domain's tables just to validate a log row's subject, mirroring appr_instance's own entity_type/entity_id loose-reference precedent.

domains/backups-ops.note: Module 20 (Backups/Ops) — built in a single comprehensive pass (small physical schema, 2 tables, but real mechanical substance: shelling out to pg_dump/pg_restore/tar, AES-256-GCM archive encryption, GFS 7/4/12 retention math, MinIO/offsite-S3 fan-out, DB/Redis/MinIO health pings, disk usage). Slug is `backups-ops` (hyphenated multi-word, matching `domains/fixed-assets`' own precedent) rather than the task brief's alternative `domains/ops` — 'ops' alone reads as broader than this module's actual scope (backups + a handful of read-only health checks), while `backups-ops` names both halves the task brief itself groups together (FR-BKP-001/003/005 all live under one 'M21. Backup & Ops (BKP)' requirements section). Three exceptions to the shared-kernel-only default, none of them a sibling `domains/*` import (same DELIBERATELY NARROW shape `domains/integrations`' own entry established — this module transmits/protects what other modules own rather than querying their data): (1) `platform/files` — `BackupOrchestratorService`/`RestoreVerificationService` inject `STORAGE_PORT` (the SAME `MinioStorageAdapter` instance `FilesModule` already wires up) via a NEW, deliberate export grant on `FilesModule` itself (`files.module.ts`'s own doc comment) — the barrel already exported the `STORAGE_PORT` token/type at the TS level, but the DI *provider* wasn't reachable cross-module until this pass added it to `exports`, the same 'barrel exports the shape, but the runtime grant still needs an explicit `exports` entry' distinction every prior cross-module grant in this codebase has hit. Bucket-level list/get (mirroring the Files bucket into a backup archive, and fetching an archive back for restore-verify) goes through a SEPARATE, backups-ops-owned `BackupStorageClient` (raw `@aws-sdk/client-s3`, same MinIO credentials via `AppConfigService`) since `StoragePort` deliberately only exposes what `FilesService` itself needs (put/sign/delete, no list/get) — extending the shared interface for one module's need was judged a bigger footprint than a small, narrowly-scoped second client reusing the same credentials. (2) `platform/settings` — `SettingsService` (generic key/value store) backs the OPTIONAL offsite-S3 destination's runtime-configurable credentials (`backups.offsite_s3.*` keys, `isSecret=true` for the access/secret key pair) — a deliberate choice over minting a new `SetIntegrationKind` enum member on `set_integration_config` (which would require altering ANOTHER module's CHECK constraint/migration for a single fixed-shape destination, a bigger footprint than this module's own scope justifies; `IntegrationConfigService`'s kind-based registry is the right fit for PLUGGABLE-ADAPTER-selection config like SMTP/SMS/accounting-sync, not a single fixed destination shape). (3) `platform/users` — listed for parity/forward-looking readiness only (same judgement call several same-sized modules make): no `bkp_*` table in this pass's DDL carries a real FK to `usr_user` (`created_by`/`updated_by` stay the standard loose uuid columns `MutableBaseEntity` always provides, no FK constraint, per this codebase's established convention for those two columns). None of `platform/files`/`platform/settings`/`platform/users` imports `domains/backups-ops` back, so none of these three is a cycle.

domainModuleDefaults.description: No domains/* modules exist yet. When one is added, register it here with this shape so the lint rule picks it up automatically.
domainModuleDefaults.note: domain modules may import accounting-core + platform + shared kernel; never another domain module's internals, only its exported service (architecture doc §3.3 rule 1)

crossSiblingImportPolicy.description: Within the same kind (e.g. two platform modules, or two future domain modules), a module may only import the sibling's public surface — its <module>.module.ts barrel / index.ts exports — never reach into another module's application, domain, or infrastructure subfolders directly.
